_comment: Advisories that `npm audit` reports but which are not reachable in this
application. Every entry must carry a justification and an expiry date.
This is NOT a way to defer work on an exploitable finding. An entry is only
legitimate when the vulnerable code path cannot be reached at all. If a fix
exists and is installable, bump the dependency instead.
Entries are checked by .github/scripts/audit-check.mjs. An expired entry is a
hard failure, so every suppression comes back for review on its own.
`workspaces` scopes an entry to the workspaces it was justified for, so a
suppression reasoned about the frontend can never silently cover the backend.

allow.title: React Router: RSC Mode CSRF Bypass Allows Action Execution Before 400 Response
reason: Applies only to React Router's RSC (React Server Components) mode, where a
server action can run before the framework returns a 400 for a rejected
request. Archivum Null's frontend is a purely client-side SPA: src/main.tsx
mounts <BrowserRouter>, and there is no SSR, no hydrateRoot, no StaticRouter
and no RSC entrypoint anywhere in frontend/src. react-router is used only for
Link, Routes, Route, useParams and useLocation. There is no server-side
rendering surface for this bypass to act on.
No fix is installable: the advisory covers react-router 7.12.0 - 8.2.0 and is
patched only in react-router 8.3.0. react-router-dom has no 8.x release - the
package was merged into react-router in v8 - so resolving this requires a
framework migration rather than a version bump.
Revisit when migrating to react-router 8.x, at which point this entry must go.
